The text says the checker starts from the seed 'when RUN begins', but only CLEAR is said to reload the PRBS states. If RUN is dropped and raised again without CLEAR, do both sequences continue or restart from 0x7FFFFFFF? When RUN falls, does the reader keep draining the FIFO? Does CLEAR (or the power-on reset) empty the FIFO, so that leftover words cannot give false data errors in the next run?
questions.answer: Both sequences restart from the seed 0x7FFFFFFF on every RUN 0 to 1, with or without CLEAR. When RUN falls, the writer stops first and the reader keeps reading until the FIFO is empty. The counters keep their values until CLEAR. CLEAR also empties the FIFO and restarts both sequences from the seed. Reset leaves the FIFO empty and both sequences at the seed.
questions.evidence: - RUN 0 to 1 starts both the writer and the reader from the seed; RUN 1 to 0 stops the writer first, then the reader keeps reading until the FIFO is empty. The counters keep their values until CLEAR.

questions.text: What is the top module name and file? In simulation, does the top expose h_we/h_re/h_addr/h_wdata/h_rdata as ports (jtag_bus excluded), or does the bench reach them some other way?
questions.topic: Names, files and the build target
questions.answer: The top-level module is `p5_async_fifo_top` in `rtl/p5_async_fifo_top.sv`. The simulation bench drives the core, `p5_async_fifo_core` in `rtl/p5_async_fifo_core.sv`, not the top. The core has the ports clk, rst (active high), h_we, h_re, h_addr[11:0], h_wdata[31:0], h_rdata[31:0] and the design's own signals. The spec does not say whether the top exposes the h_* signals as ports, because the bench does not use the top.
questions.evidence: - Names and files: the top-level module is named `p5_async_fifo_top` in `rtl/p5_async_fifo_top.sv`; the register-port core (the logic behind the `h_*` port, with no vendor primitive) is a separate module named `p5_async_fifo_core` in `rtl/p5_async_fifo_core.sv`, with ports `clk`, `rst` (active high), `h_we`, `h_re`, `h_addr[11:0]`, `h_wdata[31:0]`, `h_rdata[31:0]` and the design's own signals. Files are SystemVerilog (`.sv`). The bench drives the core.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of clk_w clocks after h_re within which h_rdata must show 0x20950001 (a number 1 or 2)? Is h_rdata required to hold that value until the next h_re? (Scenario: Host asserts h_re for one clk_w clock with h_addr=0x000 on the first clock after the 16-clock reset ends. Counted in clk_w clocks after the h_re clock, h_rdata must be valid.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Within 2 clocks at most. The spec says h_rdata must show the addressed register within 2 clocks of h_re and hold it, but it does not say how long it holds beyond 'hold it'. In particular it does not say 'until the next h_re'. The register port is in the domain of `clk`, and the spec does not use the name clk_w.
questions.evidence: After `h_re`, `h_rdata` must show the addressed register within 2 clocks and hold it.

questions.text: On each clk_w clock while full, does STALL_W increment by 1 and OVERFLOWS remain 0 (writer stalls rather than attempting the write)? (Scenario: SLOW_READ=1 and RUN=1 for a long time; the FIFO is at 512 words.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Yes. While the FIFO is full and the writer has a word to write, the writer waits, so it makes no write attempt and OVERFLOWS stays 0. STALL_W counts each such writer clock cycle, so it goes up by 1 per writer clock while the FIFO is full. This is the same answer for both readers, since the spec defines STALL_W as 'writer clock cycles in which the writer had a word to write and the FIFO was full'.
questions.evidence: - A write while full (an overflow) cannot happen because the writer waits; OVERFLOWS counts a write attempt that the FIFO rejected and must stay 0. UNDERFLOWS counts a read attempt on an empty FIFO and must stay 0. They are monitors, not behaviours.

questions.text: Does the read of 0x100 return 0 and do all mapped registers, including 0x008, remain unchanged? (Scenario: Host writes 0xFFFFFFFF to address 0x100 (unmapped) and then reads 0x100 and also reads 0x00C (between mapped registers, whose mapping is not given).) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. 0x100 is unmapped, so the write is ignored and the read returns 0. All mapped registers, including SCRATCH at 0x008, stay unchanged. 0x00C is not in any register table, so it is unmapped too and reads 0.
questions.evidence: Unmapped addresses read 0 and ignore writes.

questions.text: By how much does DATA_ERRS increase in total? (Scenario: Host writes 1 to INJECT while a received word is already differing because of an earlier injection still pending, i.e. two INJECT writes occur before the reader pops the next word.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: DATA_ERRS increases by 1 in total. The second INJECT is ignored while one is pending, so only one word is flipped and counted.
questions.evidence: INJECT flips bit 0 of the next received word before the check, once; DATA_ERRS then counts 1. A second INJECT while one is pending is ignored.

questions.text: Does either write cause a bit flip, and what does INJECT read after each? (Scenario: Host writes 0x00000000 to INJECT, then separately writes 0xFFFFFFFE (bit 0 = 0).) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Only part of this is settled. INJECT is not a register of its own; it is bit 3 of CTRL (0x010), and the flipped bit is always bit 0 of the next received word, whatever value the host writes. A write with bit 3 = 0 (0x00000000) does not request an injection. A write with bit 3 = 1 does request one, and 0xFFFFFFFE has bit 3 set. A second INJECT while one is pending is ignored. The specification does not say what INJECT reads back after either write. It only says the bit is self-clearing.
questions.evidence: | 0x010 | CTRL | RW | bit 0 RUN, bit 1 SLOW_READ, bit 2 CLEAR (self-clearing; counters and the sequences restart; only while RUN is 0), bit 3 INJECT (self-clearing; one flipped word) |

questions.text: After reset release, does register 0x008 read 0, are the FIFO contents discarded and are both PRBS states at seed 0x7FFFFFFF? (Scenario: The system is mid-run with RUN=1 and 300 words in the FIFO when rst is asserted for 16 clk_w clocks.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. Reset puts RUN at 0, SLOW_READ at 0, all counters at 0, both sequences at the seed 0x7FFFFFFF, and the FIFO empty, so the 300 words in the FIFO are discarded. SCRATCH (0x008) also resets to 0, per the register table.
questions.evidence: - Reset: RUN 0, SLOW_READ 0, all counters 0, both sequences at the seed 0x7FFFFFFF, the FIFO empty. A reset is asynchronous-assert, synchronous-release in each clock domain.

questions.text: What is led[1] on the clock after CLEAR takes effect? (Scenario: OVERFLOWS became 1 earlier so led[1]=1. RUN=0 and host writes CLEAR.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
